handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

what_was_done_this_session.eda_text_output_added: Added print() text output to 5 chart-only EDA cells so findings are machine-readable. key_eda_findings.ROW_SF_dominance: ROW_SF is the single best predictor for almost every proposal item (r>=0.93 for water main, sewer main, sidewalks, utility trenching, drywells, etc.). It outperforms both lot_count and road_LF for most items. ROW_SF is now documented as the primary analog-matching metric for M3.
key_eda_findings.drywell_rule_corrected: The drywell rule was NOT broken because drywells don't correlate with lots — it was broken because the ratio was wrong (used 1:1, actual median ratio is 0.23). Rule is now qty = max(1, round(lot_count * 0.23)), 8/10 within 50%. Small jobs floor at 2 regardless; ROW_SF is a better driver (r=0.955).
key_eda_findings.lf_items_vs_road_lf: 8" WATER MAIN: r=0.934, median 0.85x road_LF (strong). ROLLED CURB: r=0.912, median 1.43x road_LF (strong, N=5). 8" SEWER MAIN: r=0.687 (weak — use analog). CURB AND GUTTER: r=0.480 (very weak — split between C&G and rolled curb jobs).
key_eda_findings.fire_hydrants: All correlations weak-moderate (best r=0.849 vs sewer services). Not formula-able — use analog scaling. Typical range 1-4, Settlement Mtn is outlier at 9.
key_eda_findings.price_trends: 6 items warrant recency-weighting (|r|>=0.50 trend): 48" SEWER MANHOLE +7.2%/yr, IRRIGATION SLEEVES -12.9%/yr, 4" SEWER SERVICES -5.7%/yr, SINGLE DRYWELLS +3.2%/yr, INLET PROTECTION +6.7%/yr, 4" SIDEWALKS +10.6%/yr.
key_eda_findings.sewer_services_r_explanation: Sewer services r=0.632 vs lot_count (lower than expected) because Forest Grove PH2 is a Phase 2 job — 78 lots but only 19 sewer services. Phase 2 jobs break the lot_count rule. Must be flagged explicitly.

irrigation_sleeves_LF_from_lot_count: LF = lot_count * 13.0. r=0.999 from pair correlation, 4/8 within 35% (medium).
rules_fixed: drywells_from_lot_count: ratio corrected from 1.0 to 0.23. Formula now qty = max(1, round(lot_count * 0.23)). Was 0/10, now 8/10 within 50% (high).

inference_steps: 1. Classify job type and scale from extracted facts
2. Select 2-3 closest analog jobs by ROW_SF (primary) and lot_count (secondary)
3. For each line item category: apply formula rule if one exists, else scale from analog by ROW_SF ratio
4. Apply derivation rules: sewer/water services = lot_count, manholes = sewer_LF/250, drywells = lot_count*0.23, water_main = road_LF*0.85, etc.
5. Apply LS formulas: strip_CY = ROW_SF*(depth/12)/27 at $2.81/CY, subgrade = road_subgrade_SY*$1.43, paving = road_paving_SY*$25.56
6. Price each item using knowledge_pack unit_price_distributions (median, recency-weight where flagged)
7. Sum to total with confidence band

analog_retrieval_note: ROW_SF is the best single similarity metric. Match analogs by ROW_SF first. Scale unknown quantities as: est_qty = analog_qty * (new_ROW_SF / analog_ROW_SF). This outperforms lot_count or road_LF scaling for nearly all items.
open_questions_for_m3: Which Woodman plan sheet is most informative for a single-sheet test? page_01.jpg (cover — lot count, firm, location) vs a plan/profile sheet (stationing). Try page_01 first.
Drywells rule still has floor-clustering behavior for small jobs (2 drywells regardless of lots). M3 should flag this and use analog for small jobs.
Fire hydrants have no reliable formula — analog-only. Range 1-9, typical 1-4.
Rolled curb vs C&G is mutually exclusive per job. M3 needs to detect curb type from Gemini extraction before applying curb rule.
Phase 2 jobs (Forest Grove PH2): lot_count rules break. M3 should detect 'Phase 2' language on the sheet and apply a correction.
